display.title: A Yud-Tes Kislev Farbrengen with a Puppet Friend: The Alter Rebbe and the Nickel
display.summary_short: At a lively pre-Yud-Tes Kislev gathering, Rabbi Goldstein and a cheeky puppet sing, say pesukim and tell how a 'thank you' for one nickel freed a jailed groom.
display.summary_long: Recorded at a gathering for older boys on Yud-Daled Kislev, a few days before Yud-Tes Kislev, Rabbi Goldstein is joined by a playful puppet who keeps getting things mixed up: is it Chanukah? Purim? They sing together, including 'I Believe in Hashem', and Rabbi Goldstein explains that Hashem holds our hand and watches us every moment, so we never need to be afraid. The puppet is reminded to say Modeh Ani, the group repeats the pasuk 'Torah tziva' together as a Hakhel gathering, and everyone sings 'We Want Moshiach Now'. Then comes a bedtime story: when a police chief jails a groom before his wedding, the Alter Rebbe collects 1,500 rubles to free him, starting with a rich man known for giving only a nickel. The Alter Rebbe thanks him warmly, and the man, delighted that someone finally accepted his gift, gives more and more until he gives the whole sum. At the wedding the cruel police chief's end is announced, and the groom later finds the money in a lost wallet. The puppet thanks everyone and asks to be invited again.
display.lesson: When you appreciate even a small thing someone does, they want to do more and more; and Hashem is always holding our hand.

date.note: 'Now is Yud-Daled Kislev... Yud-Tes Kislev is next Tuesday... tomorrow's Friday'; Hakhel mentioned, so 5769, 5776 or 5783 (14 Kislev falls on Thursday in each).

advisories.note: The cruel police chief falls off his horse and dies; the townspeople are relieved.
A groom is jailed before his wedding until he is ransomed.

characters: Moshe, the rich man who gave a nickel
